problem: Communicating complex system designs and scientific processes through text alone is inefficient and prone to ambiguity.
approach: Leverages language models to generate intermediate DOT code from text descriptions, then processes it to create high-fidelity architecture diagrams; fine-tunes small LMs and uses in-context learning with GPT-4o.
contribution: Introduces Text2Arch dataset with scientific architecture images, textual descriptions, and DOT code; fine-tuned models significantly outperform DiagramAgent and match GPT-4o performance.

problem: Vision-language models like CLIP exhibit test-time adaptation bias from pretraining on imbalanced data, leading to biased entropy estimates of uncertainty.
approach: Generalizes Shannon Entropy to Tsallis Entropy with adaptive class-specific parameters derived from estimated label bias; integrates with label adjustment for test-time adaptation.
contribution: Proposes Adaptive Debiasing Tsallis Entropy (ADTE) that outperforms state-of-the-art on ImageNet and 10 cross-domain benchmarks without hyperparameter tuning.

problem: Machine unlearning on non-linear models like neural networks suffers from degenerate Hessians, making batch and sequential unlearning inefficient with large update norms.
approach: Applies cubic regularization to Newton's method to address degeneracy while enabling efficient batch and sequential unlearning with automatic regularization.
contribution: Proposes unlearning algorithms achieving competitive performance in both batch and sequential settings on real-world datasets without manual hyperparameter tuning.

problem: Large language model scaling is bottlenecked by data scarcity and performance degradation from excessive data repetition during training.
approach: Introduces Massive Genre-Audience (MGA) reformulation framework that systematically augments corpora into diverse contextually-rich variations via adaptive genre-audience pair generation; produces 770 billion token MGACorpus.
contribution: Demonstrates superior scaling properties up to 13B parameters against data repetition and upsampling baselines.

problem: Guiding diffusion-based planners in reactive closed-loop autonomous driving environments remains challenging; simple conditioning fails in complex dynamic scenarios.
approach: Introduces BridgeDrive, an anchor-guided diffusion bridge policy that translates driving behavior anchors into fine-grained trajectory plans via a principled diffusion framework compatible with efficient ODE solvers.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on Bench2Drive benchmark, improving success rate by 7.72% over prior work.

problem: Bilevel optimization is intractable for general convex lower-level functions; existing methods assume strong convexity or Polyak-Łojasiewicz conditions.
approach: Identifies uniformly convex lower-level functions as a tractable class interpolating between strong convexity and general convexity; develops UniBiO algorithm with cubic regularization and implicit differentiation.
contribution: Establishes novel implicit differentiation theorem and achieves O(ε^{-5p+6}) oracle complexity matching optimal rates for strongly convex functions up to log factors.

problem: Body composition analysis via CT/MRI for cardio-metabolic health remains limited by accessibility barriers including radiation, cost, and infrastructure requirements.
approach: Develops AbdCTBench dataset of 23,506 CT-derived abdominal surface meshes paired with comorbidity labels and biomarkers; benchmarks seven vision architectures on surface-to-biomarker prediction.
contribution: Demonstrates surface geometry is predictive of internal tissue composition; best models achieve age prediction MAE 6.22 years (R²=0.757), mortality AUROC 0.839, diabetes detection AUROC 0.801.

problem: Bundle construction via sequential item prediction is fundamentally unsuitable for unordered bundles; faces exponential combination complexity and curse of dimensionality.
approach: Proposes DDBC, a discrete diffusion model for non-sequential bundle construction using masked denoising; integrates residual vector quantization to compress embeddings into discrete codes reducing catalog size.
contribution: Achieves over 1× improvement on music playlist continuation and fashion outfit completion benchmarks.

problem: Cryo-EM reconstruction relies on external consensus maps or atomic models for initialization; existing Gaussian mixture model methods are incompatible with differentiable rendering and cryo-EM physics.
approach: Proposes cryoSplat integrating Gaussian splatting with cryo-EM physics via orthogonal projection-aware rendering, view-dependent normalization, and FFT-aligned coordinates for self-contained reconstruction.
contribution: Enables stable and efficient homogeneous reconstruction directly from raw cryo-EM particles without external initialization.

problem: Backdoor attacks on LLMs via model editing suffer from safety fallback, where models initially respond affirmatively but later revert to refusals due to safety alignment.
approach: Proposes DualEdit dual-objective framework jointly promoting affirmative outputs and suppressing refusal responses via dynamic loss weighting and refusal value anchoring to cluster representative refusal vectors.
contribution: Improves attack success by 9.98% and reduces safety fallback rate by 10.88% over baselines.

problem: Single-pass LLM reasoning in multi-hop QA is bottlenecked by finite per-pass output capacity; integrating task-relevant evidence becomes unreliable once capacity is exceeded.
approach: Establishes Fano-style accuracy upper bound formalizing capacity limits; proposes InfoQA framework combining capacity-aware task decomposition with active pruning to maintain information load within single-pass limits.
contribution: Model behavior aligns with predicted capacity curves; InfoQA achieves consistent performance improvements on stringent noise-rich benchmark.

problem: Vision encoders in MLLMs lack fine-grained regional analysis; fine-grained perception is limited by scarcity of annotated data and lack of pretraining paradigm.
approach: Constructs Gran-29M dataset of 29 million images with 180 million region-level annotations; develops GranViT vision transformer with region-level autoregressive training and self-distillation for fine-grained feature extraction.
contribution: GranViT surpasses existing vision encoders with strong transferability to MLLM tasks.

problem: Grounding high-level robot task plans into executable actions remains challenging with limited high-quality robot data availability.
approach: Proposes HinFlow combining online rollouts with retrospective goal annotation from achieved outcomes and hindsight relabeling to update goal-conditioned imitation policy; uses 2D point flows as high-level planner.
contribution: Achieves more than 2× performance improvement over base policy; enables policy acquisition from cross-embodiment video data.

problem: Evaluating MLLMs' visual emotion perception is constrained by overlooking plausible responses, limited emotional taxonomies, neglect of contextual factors, and labor-intensive annotations.
approach: Proposes Emotion Statement Judgment task for customized evaluation; develops automated pipeline efficiently constructing emotion-centric statements with minimal human effort.
contribution: Comprehensive MLLM assessment reveals stronger performance in emotion interpretation but significant gaps versus humans, especially on perception subjectivity.

problem: Applying group-invariant Bellman backups in real-world environments with local symmetry-breaking causes errors that propagate globally, reducing value estimation accuracy.
approach: Introduces Partially group-Invariant MDP (PI-MDP) selectively applying group-invariant or standard backups depending on where symmetry holds; develops PE-DQN and PE-SAC algorithms.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines on Grid-World, locomotion, and manipulation benchmarks, demonstrating benefits of selective symmetry exploitation.

problem: Training LLMs on long contexts is severely constrained by prohibitive GPU memory overhead from activation and KV cache scaling linearly with sequence length.
approach: Introduces OOMB training system using chunk-recurrent framework with on-the-fly activation recomputation maintaining O(1) memory; integrates paged memory manager, asynchronous CPU offloading, and page-level sparse attention.
contribution: Enables training Qwen2.5-7B with 4M-token context on single H200 GPU; adds only 10MB memory per 10K additional tokens.

problem: Deep learning has non-convex loss landscape making optimization dynamics hard to analyze and control; precise learning rate scaling remains unclear.
approach: Examines when deep learning exhibits weakly convex behavior; builds scaling laws of learning rates and losses based on convexity principles.
contribution: Demonstrates learning rate scaling laws that extrapolate 80× across training horizons and 70× across model sizes.

problem: Reward models inherit value biases from base pretrained LLMs despite being designed to represent human preferences.
approach: Comprehensive study of 10 open-weight reward models using psycholinguistic corpora; traces value differences to logits of instruction-tuned and pretrained base models; derives implicit reward scores.
contribution: Shows Llama RMs prefer 'agency' and Gemma RMs prefer 'communion' robustly; effect durable despite identical preference data and finetuning.

problem: Non-prehensile manipulation with dexterous multi-fingered hands remains underexplored, lacking contact-aware datasets and wrist-finger control policies.
approach: Presents DexMove combining scalable simulation pipeline generating physically plausible trajectories with wearable device capturing multi-finger contact via vision-based tactile sensors; trains flow-based policy for real-time control.
contribution: Successfully manipulated six objects with 77.8% success rate; outperforms baselines by 36.6% and improves efficiency by 300%.

problem: LLMs remain static post-training, unable to dynamically adapt weights in response to continuous streams of new information at inference time.
approach: Introduces In-Place TTT framework treating final MLP projection matrices as adaptable fast weights; replaces reconstruction objective with next-token-prediction-aligned objective and efficient chunk-wise updates.
contribution: Enables 4B-parameter model to achieve superior performance on 128K context tasks; consistently outperforms TTT-related approaches when pretrained.

problem: Integrating diverse knowledge from heterogeneous models including visual generatives, language models, and physics simulators for controllable synthesis remains underexplored.
approach: Proposes probabilistic framework combining heterogeneous expert models via product distribution; introduces annealed MCMC sampler with SMC-style resampling for efficient inference-time composition.
contribution: Achieves better controllability than monolithic methods for image and video synthesis tasks with flexible user interfaces.

problem: Equivariant neural networks suffer degraded expressivity when processing symmetric inputs due to symmetry increase; comprehensive reduction strategies remain lacking.
approach: Provides rigorous characterization of symmetry increase and develops computable algorithm deriving infimum of increased symmetry; proposes practical guidelines for feature design.
contribution: Proves increased symmetry admits infimum determined by feature space structure; validates theoretical predictions on synthetic and QM9 real-world dataset.

problem: Enforcing complex nonconvex operational constraints in learning and control systems remains challenging; existing methods struggle with efficiency and reliability.
approach: Proposes data-driven amortized approach using trained autoencoder with adversarial objective as approximate projector; learns structured convex latent representation enabling fast corrections to infeasible predictions.
contribution: Effectively improves constraint satisfaction at low computational cost on constrained optimization and RL problems with nonconvex constraints.

problem: Existing positional encoding methods for transformers lack theoretical clarity and rely on limited evaluation metrics for context length extrapolation claims.
approach: Proposes Bayesian Attention Mechanism (BAM) formalizing positional encoding as prior within probabilistic model; introduces Generalized Gaussian positional prior improving long-context generalization.
contribution: Enables accurate information retrieval at 500× training context length, outperforming prior work by 25× in retrieval accuracy.

problem: Medical MLLMs underperform in zero-shot medical image interpretation; visual grounding in clinically relevant regions remains poorly understood.
approach: Introduces VGMED evaluation dataset assessing visual grounding capability with expert clinical guidance; proposes VGRefine inference-time method refining attention distribution for medical settings.
contribution: Achieves SOTA on 6 diverse Med-VQA benchmarks without additional training; demonstrates medical MLLMs often fail to ground predictions in clinically relevant regions.

problem: Estimating causal effects becomes challenging when outcomes possess complex non-Euclidean structures; conventional approaches fail to capture meaningful structural variation.
approach: Introduces topological causal inference framework defining treatment effects through changes in underlying topological structure; uses power-weighted silhouettes to summarize intervention-driven topological shifts.
contribution: Proposes doubly robust estimator with asymptotic properties and formal test for null hypothesis; reliably quantifies treatment effects across diverse outcome spaces.

problem: Generative modeling on convex domains using flow matching faces challenges from heavy-tailed dual distributions and poor coupling with Gaussian priors.
approach: Proposes Mirror Flow Matching using regularized mirror map controlling dual tail behavior and Student-t prior aligning with heavy-tailed targets; provides spatial Lipschitzness and temporal regularity guarantees.
contribution: Achieves spatial Lipschitzness and Wasserstein convergence; outperforms baselines on synthetic convex-domain simulations and real-world constrained generation tasks.

problem: Drug-target interaction prediction relies primarily on SMILES-protein pairs, failing to exploit rich multimodal information available for molecules and proteins.
approach: Introduces GRAM-DTI pre-training framework integrating multimodal molecule and protein inputs via volume-based contrastive learning to four modalities; proposes adaptive modality dropout and incorporates IC50 weak supervision.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on four public datasets, highlighting benefits of higher-order multimodal alignment and adaptive modality utilization.

problem: Evaluating LLM reasoning on graph-theoretic tasks lacks comprehensive benchmark spanning diverse graph types, serialization formats, and prompting schemes.
approach: Introduces GraphOmni comprehensive benchmark with diverse graph types and formats; uncovers critical interactions among dimensions affecting performance; introduces RL-based optimizer adaptively selecting factor combinations.
contribution: Reveals closed-source models like Claude-3.5 lead overall but leave headroom; reduces evaluation cost by 75% via adaptive factor selection while retaining accuracy.

problem: Embodied intelligence requires high-fidelity simulation environments but existing platforms suffer from data contamination and limited flexibility.
approach: Proposes World2Minecraft converting real-world scenes to structured Minecraft environments via 3D semantic occupancy prediction; introduces automated data pipeline for creating customized occupancy datasets.
contribution: Introduces MinecraftOcc dataset with 100,165 images from 156 detailed indoor scenes; demonstrates dataset improves occupancy prediction and provides customizable embodied AI research platform.

problem: Text-to-image models fail handling complex spatial relationships; current benchmarks overlook spatial reasoning due to short or information-sparse prompt design.
approach: Introduces SpatialGenEval benchmark with 1,230 long information-dense prompts across 25 scenes covering 10 spatial sub-domains; constructs SpatialT2I dataset with 15,400 text-image pairs preserving consistency and information density.
contribution: Reveals higher-order spatial reasoning as primary bottleneck; fine-tuned models show consistent gains (+4.2% to +5.7%) with more realistic spatial relations.

problem: Applying LLMs to long texts via divide-and-conquer chunking shows unclear conditions for effectiveness; failure modes are poorly understood.
approach: Proposes noise decomposition framework distinguishing failures into three categories: cross-chunk dependence (task noise), context-size confusion (model noise), and aggregator imperfection (aggregator noise); analyzes when multi-agent chunking is effective.
contribution: Explains why weaker chunked models can surpass advanced single-shot models on long inputs; identifies tractable chunking conditions via principled framework.

problem: LLMs contain inactive attention heads providing computational redundancy; systematic methods for identifying and evaluating inactivity remain limited.
approach: Proposes taxonomy of 12 score functions measuring different ways heads are inactive; evaluates inactive heads via model interventions; finds output-norm-based scores better identify inactivity than attention-weight scores.
contribution: Shows over 12% of attention heads average inactive; can be ablated while maintaining accuracy, revealing attention sinks underestimate inactivity by 7%.

problem: Lipschitz bandit problem lacks methods for handling stochastic delayed feedback; rewards observed after random delays complicate learning.
approach: Designs delay-aware zooming algorithm for bounded delays and phased learning strategy for unbounded delays; establishes regret lower bound for unbounded case.
contribution: Achieves sublinear regret in both bounded and unbounded delay settings; optimal rates with bounded delays up to maximum delay term.

problem: Local gradient-based optimization methods provide no global information about objective landscape, leading to suboptimal convergence and initialization sensitivity.
approach: Leverages resurgence theory from complex analysis extracting global structural information via partition function computation; identifies Borel transform singularities corresponding to critical objective values.
contribution: Provides theoretically-grounded global guidance to local optimizers; enables principled learning rate adaptation and escape from suboptimal regions.

problem: Knowledge editing in code-related tasks suffers from neuronal polysemanticity in MLP layers, hindering precision and interpretability of parameter edits.
approach: Introduces TCPE exploiting sparsity and monosemanticity of TransCoder neurons for localized code knowledge editing; creates KECode evaluation benchmark for code-to-code translation.
contribution: Achieves neuron-level mechanistic interpretability with precise correspondence between edited neurons and specific code knowledge; systematically evaluates KE methods.

problem: Local loss geometry considering only single loss is fully summarized by spectrum; however, both training and test losses are relevant, requiring eigenspace alignment understanding.
approach: Establishes foundations for two-loss geometry via universal fluctuation law combining spectral data with eigenspace overlap; proves transfer law describing overlap transformations; applies to ridge regression with covariate shift.
contribution: Reveals eigenspace alignment as controlling multiple descent peaks rather than Hessian ill-conditioning; develops algorithms estimating overlap functionals validated on ResNet-20 and CIFAR10.

problem: Current earth observation agent frameworks lack capability for complex multi-step reasoning, remain confined to RGB perception, and lack systematic evaluation protocols.
approach: Introduces Earth-Agent agentic framework unifying RGB and spectral EO data via MCP-based tool ecosystem; proposes Earth-Bench benchmark with 248 expert-curated tasks.
contribution: Enables complex scientific tasks like geophysical parameter retrieval and quantitative spatiotemporal analysis beyond pretrained MLLMs; establishes new paradigm for scientifically grounded EO analysis.

problem: Lightweight neural networks suffer low-frequency bias due to constrained capacity, limiting ability to capture fine-grained high-frequency details like textures and edges.
approach: Performs systematic frequency analysis of gating mechanisms showing GLU interplay amplifies high-frequency signals; introduces GmNet incorporating frequency-aware gating into lightweight backbone.
contribution: Achieves new state-of-the-art for efficient models without complex training strategies or architectural search.

problem: Realistic talking-head video generation struggles with nuanced emotional expressions due to lack of fine-grained emotion control.
approach: Proposes two-stage AUHead method disentangling Action Units (AUs) from audio via spatial-temporal tokenization and AU-driven diffusion model; introduces AU disentanglement guidance for quality trade-off.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance in emotional realism, accurate lip synchronization, and visual coherence, significantly surpassing existing techniques.
